svg.text: Round-end admission: range order kept, resident records left in place
G = 3 resident slots. During round r, A splits at 4 and B at 12; their right halves are copied into newTasks, each recording its parent’s position in the
round order. endRound stages indices, admits the first G, pushes the rest onto pending in reverse order and fills freed slots with copies of selected new tasks.
three resident tasks; order = [0, 1, 2] visits slots 0, 1, 2
A keeps the left half [0, 4) in slot 0; B keeps [8, 12) in slot 1. “parent” is the parent’s
position in the round order, not its slot. Each new task hints its first access at creation.
each new right sibling is interleaved right after its surviving left half; encodings below G name slots, others name newTasks entries
copied to pending in reverse, so the earliest range is on top and resumes first
A suspended task is a copy; it keeps its list cursors and search bounds. When it resumes, the access
its state consumes is hinted again: whatever was prefetched before may have been evicted.
Slot 2 is freed only after C has been copied out, so a selected new task can take it.
A-left and B-left were never moved; A-right was copied into the freed slot 2; order = [0, 2, 1] restores range order
visits A-left, then A-right, then B-left: [0, 4), [4, 8), [8, 12)
B-right and C resume, in that order, as slots free up in later rounds.
What this buys, and what it does not
Range priority survives suspension: the task with the earliest unresolved reads is always among the resident ones, and the pending stack hands back
the next-earliest first. Selected resident tasks are never copied: endRound moves indices, then copies only the suspended suffix and the selected new tasks.
A new task never runs in the round that created it. Its first visit occurs in a later round after admission; a task resumed from pending hints
This is not a uniform round-robin: a visit can be a whole leaf scan, and a task can be deep in a child while another is still partitioning higher up.
The scheme does not avoid copies of suspended and new records; a stable pool of task objects was considered and left out of this version.
